terms.grammar: phrase: crēdō with in and the accusative
evidence: Vulg. Jo. 6.35: quī crēdit in mē
terms.comment: The construction of Christian Latin, and of the Creed, Crēdō in ūnum Deum. Augustine marks the difference: believing that Christ exists is Chrīstum esse crēdere, believing in him is in Chrīstum crēdere.

evidence: Cic. Div. 1.104: id ipsum est deōs nōn putāre (Lewis & Short, s.v. putō)
terms.comment: The classical way, of the pagan gods: to hold that they exist and to heed their signs.

phrases.english: I believe, Lord; help my unbelief.
phrases.source: Vulg. Mc. 9.23 (the Stuttgart text omits Domine)

phrases.latin: et quī crēdit in mē, nōn sitiet umquam
phrases.english: and whoever believes in me will never thirst

phrases.latin: Chrīstum esse crēdit, nōn in Chrīstum crēdit
phrases.english: (whoever has faith without hope and love) believes that Christ is, not in Christ

sources: Lewis & Short: credo · Lewis & Short: puto
Scripture from the Latinitas collection of prayers (preces), checked against the Clementine Vulgate, with the Stuttgart reading noted where its words differ.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
